render:
Fresh chat for each task
  Rule: One task per chat; clear between unrelated tasks. Clearing is free.
  Why:  Every turn re-sends the whole conversation; calls over 150K context were 75% of one heavy week (dotclaude).
  Claude Code  /clear (then /rename and /resume to come back)
  Codex        /new
  Antigravity  /clear (/new)
  Cursor       /clear (/new)

Compacting is not free
  Rule: Compact only a chat you must keep, at a natural boundary, with instructions; prefer a handoff plus a fresh chat.
  Why:  /compact reads the whole conversation to write its summary: a large request itself (Anthropic cost guide).
  Claude Code  /compact keep: goal, files, failing test
  Codex        /compact
  Antigravity  fresh chat + handoff
  Cursor       /summarize
  askai:       askai break, then a fresh chat

One complete prompt
  Rule: Send one prompt with the goal, the files and how to verify; do not drip-feed follow-ups.
  Why:  Each extra message is another full re-read of the context (dotclaude; AI LABS; your screenshot page 1).

Edit instead of correcting
  Rule: If an answer is slightly wrong, edit your message and regenerate rather than sending a correction.
  Why:  Follow-ups stay in history and are re-sent every turn (your screenshot page 1).
  Claude Code  Esc Esc to edit the previous message
  Codex        Esc Esc (edit and fork)
  Antigravity  /rewind
  Cursor       /rewind

Point at files
  Rule: Name the file and function with @path; avoid "improve the codebase".
  Why:  Vague prompts trigger broad scanning (Anthropic); @ targeting minimises token overhead (Antigravity docs).

Plan before multi-file edits
  Rule: Use plan mode for anything touching more than two files and approve before edits.
  Why:  A wrong path costs the work twice (Anthropic, Antigravity, Cursor docs; screenshot page 2).
  Claude Code  Shift+Tab or /plan
  Codex        /plan
  Antigravity  /plan, /planning
  Cursor       /plan, /ask

Give a verification target
  Rule: Give a test, command or expected output that proves the task is done.
  Why:  Agents that can check their own work need fewer correction rounds (Anthropic, Antigravity best practices).

One round of questions
  Rule: Ask for one round of clarifying questions, then proceed.
  Why:  Open-ended question loops add turns; your screenshot page 2 rule kept to one round.

Stop wrong turns early
  Rule: Press Esc as soon as the agent drifts, then rewind instead of arguing.
  Why:  All four vendors document it; every extra wrong step is re-read later.
  Claude Code  Esc, /rewind
  Codex        Esc, Esc Esc
  Antigravity  Esc, /rewind (/undo)
  Cursor       Esc, /rewind

Paste only what matters
  Rule: Paste the failing function or the last 10-40 log lines, not the whole log.
  Why:  Your screenshot page 5; Anthropic filters test output to failures in its hook example.

Search, then read ranges
  Rule: Search first, then read only the needed line ranges; batch independent reads in one message.
  Why:  Reads were 90.6% of tool-result tokens in one workload (Marmelab); parallel calls cost one turn (dotclaude).
  askai:       askai install writes this rule for every host

Smallest change that works
  Rule: Ask for the smallest change that solves the task; no speculative features or unrequested refactors.
  Why:  Ponytail measured -10.3% cost, quality unchanged (JetBrains, p=0.004).
  askai:       askai install writes the build-lean rule for every host

Terse replies
  Rule: Ask for terse answers: no preamble or narration; exact code and errors.
  Why:  Caveman-style rules: median -8% cost over six studies, quality unchanged.
  askai:       askai install writes the terse block (--caveman lite|full|ultra|off)

Few, cheap subagents
  Rule: Use subagents only for broad searches or logs, on a cheap model; no agent teams for routine work.
  Why:  Teams use about 7x tokens (Anthropic); each fresh subagent writes ~14K tokens before its first call (dotclaude).
  Claude Code  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku
  Codex        [agents] default_subagent_reasoning_effort = "medium"
  Antigravity  Flash for background subagents
  askai:       askai install sets the subagent model

Short instruction files
  Rule: Keep CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md under 200 lines, as an index; move workflows into skills.
  Why:  They load every session and every subagent (Anthropic); Codex caps at 32 KiB; Antigravity always-on rules share 20K tokens.
  askai:       askai check measures them

Unused MCP servers off
  Rule: Disable MCP servers you do not use today; prefer CLIs like gh, rg and jq.
  Why:  Each server adds tool names and instructions to every session (Anthropic cost guide).
  Claude Code  /mcp
  Codex        /mcp
  Antigravity  /mcp or "disabled": true in mcp_config.json
  Cursor       Settings, MCP
  askai:       askai check counts servers

Convert documents first
  Rule: Convert PDFs, Office files and HTML to Markdown before attaching.
  Why:  Binary documents cost far more tokens than their text.
  askai:       askai install --profile docs installs markitdown

Claude Code models
  Rule: Haiku for search and small edits, Sonnet for everyday work, Opus (or Sonnet + /advisor opus) only for the hard step.
  Why:  A model switch is the only repeated large saving in the benchmarks; Claude Code defaults to Opus since 22 Sep 2026.
  Claude Code  /model haiku|sonnet|opus
  askai:       askai install sets a cheap default when none is set

Codex models
  Rule: A Luna-class model for routine work, Sol for hard tasks; start fresh before 272K input tokens.
  Why:  Published Plus estimates: Luna 350-3,000 messages per 5 h, Sol 15-160; inputs past 272K bill input at 2x.
  Codex        /model
  askai:       askai install --codex-model NAME

Antigravity models
  Rule: Flash for routine work; Pro or Claude for hard tasks; quota is per model, so switch when one runs out.
  Why:  Antigravity plans page; Flash has its own pool that refreshes more often.
  Antigravity  /model, /usage (/quota)

Cursor models and Auto
  Rule: Auto for routine work; a frontier model only for the hard task; Max Mode off.
  Why:  Cursor pricing: Auto bills $1.25/M input, $6/M output, $0.25/M cache reads, cheaper than frontier models but not free.
  Cursor       model picker; Dashboard, Usage

High effort for Claude, medium elsewhere
  Rule: Claude Code defaults to high effort. Use max only for the hard step. Codex and Antigravity stay on medium.
  Why:  Thinking is billed as output (Anthropic); one creator measured max effort at 3.5-4x tokens.
  Claude Code  /effort high
  Codex        Alt+, / Alt+.
  Antigravity  /effort low|medium
  askai:       askai install sets high effort for Claude Code and medium for Codex

Advisor instead of Opus
  Rule: For a hard task, keep a Sonnet session and run /advisor opus instead of switching to Opus.
  Why:  The advisor is consulted at decision points; analyses put it about a third cheaper than Opus throughout.
  Claude Code  /advisor opus

No speed or big-context modes
  Rule: Leave Claude fast mode, Codex Fast/Ultrafast, Cursor Max Mode and Antigravity /boost off unless speed matters more.
  Why:  They spend allowance faster: fast mode bills credits at 2x; Codex Fast 2.5x, Ultrafast 8x.

Avoid Claude peak hours for big jobs
  Rule: Run big refactors and long agent runs outside weekdays 08:00-14:00 US Eastern.
  Why:  Anthropic, March 2026: the 5-hour window drains faster at peak (your screenshot page 9).
  askai:       askai tips peak

Before a break
  Rule: Finish the verified step, commit or stash, ask the agent to write .ai-work/HANDOFF.md, stop loops, goals and background agents.
  Why:  Background work keeps spending; the cache expires after 1 h (5 min on usage credits).
  askai:       askai break

Coming back
  Rule: Within the cache lifetime and with a small context, continue; otherwise start fresh from the handoff.
  Why:  The first message after the cache expires re-processes the whole conversation (Anthropic).
  Claude Code  claude -c or a fresh chat
  Codex        codex resume --last
  Antigravity  /resume
  Cursor       agent --continue
  askai:       askai resume (prints the prompt; --copy copies it)

When you hit a limit
  Rule: Wait for the reset, switch model family after a model-specific limit, or switch to a model with its own pool.
  Why:  Claude: /model sonnet after an Opus limit; Codex: /usage shows resets; Antigravity: Flash pool; Cursor: Auto.

Billing traps
  Rule: Unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY unless you mean to pay per token; keep Antigravity credits off.
  Why:  An API key overrides your plan; Headroom-style proxies showed "API Usage Billing" (your screenshot page 18).
  askai:       askai check and askai doctor flag them

RTK
  Rule: Not recommended by default: measure on your own work if you try it.
  Why:  Median +7% task cost over six third-party studies; its counter logged 96M tokens saved in runs that cost 7.6% more.
  askai:       askai install --rtk (opt-in)

Context Mode
  Rule: Not recommended by default.
  Why:  The one paired study measured +33% to +72% cost.
  askai:       askai install --context-mode (opt-in)

Headroom
  Rule: Installed with --headroom or the max profile in MCP mode: the agent calls headroom_compress on large outputs. Proxy mode (headroom wrap, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) is not set up by AskAI.
  Why:  Vendor reports 47-92% on large tool outputs; four independent studies found a median +32% cost; proxy mode moved Claude Code to API billing in your screenshot.
  Claude Code  headroom_stats inside the session
  askai:       askai install --headroom; askai infra shows where it is registered

Proxies and routers
  Rule: Avoid on a subscription.
  Why:  Proxies can switch billing, break the prompt cache and send code to third parties.

Code navigation plugins
  Rule: Install the official code-intelligence plugin for typed languages.
  Why:  LSP navigation measured -13% cost (Marmelab); Anthropic recommends it.
  Claude Code  /plugin install typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official
  askai:       askai install --lsp ts,py

Usage jumps while idle
  Rule: Compare /stats in the CLI with claude.ai's usage bar; report a mismatch.
  Why:  Reported counter-desync bug (GitHub issues #38335, #39507).

Keep junk out of Cursor
  Rule: Add .cursorignore for node_modules, build output, lockfiles, .env and large data.
  Why:  Cursor indexes and reads what it can see; ignored files cost nothing.
  askai:       askai scaffold writes it; askai check looks for it

Codex: local before cloud
  Rule: Run small jobs locally; ask for several cloud attempts only when you will compare them.
  Why:  OpenAI says cloud tasks can use more of the allowance; each attempt is its own run.

Nest AGENTS.md by folder
  Rule: Put a service's rules in its own folder's AGENTS.md so they load only there.
  Why:  Codex reads AGENTS.md from the repo root down to the current folder (OpenAI).

SuperClaude
  Rule: Optional: its --uc mode is a terse-output rule like Caveman; the framework itself loads several thousand tokens of instructions every session.
  Why:  Claims 30-50% fewer tokens with --uc; no third-party measurement found; one analysis lists ~1.6K tokens of commands and ~2.3K of flags loaded by its CLAUDE.md imports.
  askai:       askai installs a short terse block instead

Doctor and audit tools
  Rule: Run the built-in /doctor weekly; askai check covers tokens and billing for all four tools; LLM-based config audits cost tokens each run.
  Why:  Built-in /doctor flags large CLAUDE.md files, agent descriptions over 15K tokens and MCP tools over 25K. claude-config-doctor is an LLM skill (costs tokens); claude-doctor analyses transcripts offline and writes rules.
  Claude Code  /doctor (press f to fix)
  askai:       askai check, askai doctor

Status lines and monitors
  Rule: Keep one status line showing context and cache; monitors show where tokens go but save nothing by themselves.
  Why:  ccstatusline, CCometixLine, claude-powerline, claude-hud and Token Monitor (26+ tools including Codex, Cursor and Antigravity) are measurement tools.
  Claude Code  /statusline
  askai:       askai installs its own status line

Budget guards
  Rule: A budget guard can warn before the weekly cap; it does not reduce tokens per task.
  Why:  tokenlens reads Claude Code session logs (exact usage) and can allow, warn, ask or deny tool calls against your weekly cap.

Offloading reads to subagents
  Rule: Moving reads into a subagent shrinks the main context, not the bill: the subagent's tokens are still spent.
  Why:  TokenRoll's scout claims 83% less main context; each fresh subagent writes ~14K tokens before its first call (dotclaude). Worth it only for very large reads.

All-in-one token plugins
  Rule: Prefer settings and short rules; bundles that inject rules through SessionStart hooks add text to every session.
  Why:  context_guard (14 skills, hooks) and token-saver (rules, cheap subagents, audit) publish no third-party measurement; their sound parts match what askai already sets.

Long chats are the biggest cost
  Rule: Keep sessions to one task; let project files carry the context so /clear costs nothing.
  Why:  Every turn re-sends the whole conversation; turns over 150K tokens were 75% of one measured heavy week (dotclaude).
  askai:       askai init writes the project files; askai clear checks the handoff first

Project files instead of chat history
  Rule: Keep a small router (AGENTS.md) pointing to PROJECT_MAP, ARCHITECTURE, FEATURES, WORK_ORDER and the handoff; after /clear the agent reads only what the task needs.
  Why:  A cleared session that reads a 40-line handoff and two files costs far less than a long chat re-sent every turn.
  askai:       askai init, askai map

What breaks the prompt cache
  Rule: Choose the model and MCP servers before the session and keep them; compact rarely.
  Why:  A model switch, connecting or disconnecting an MCP server, a plugin that adds MCP tools, compaction and fast mode rebuild the cache; an effort change keeps it (Anthropic). Legacy env names still seen in the wild, not recommended: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M.
  Claude Code  askai go claude --tier build
  askai:       askai go, askai audit (shows switches and cache share)

Limit tool output
  Rule: Cap, grep or summarise output before it reaches the chat: quiet flags, tail -n 40, only failing lines.
  Why:  Bash output above the cap is never read; AskAI sets bashOutputMaxChars to 15,000. Hooks that rewrite commands measured no net saving (RTK).
  askai:       askai prompt --output-safe "cmd"

Prompt modifiers
  Rule: Add one modifier line instead of a long instruction: BLUNT, BRUTAL, ASSUME, COUNTER, CONTRAST.
  Why:  One line replaces several turns of back-and-forth when you want a direct critique.
  askai:       askai prompt --mode brutal

Graphify
  Rule: Optional for very large repos: build the graph once and point the agent at GRAPH_REPORT.md.
  Why:  Claims 71.5x fewer tokens per query; an independent test saw ~0% when the agent ignored the graph; building it costs tokens; its Claude hook fires on every search.
  askai:       askai plugins install graphify; askai map links the report

Graftcode rules
  Rule: In a project that uses Graftcode, add its rules so agents call methods through generated packages instead of writing REST code.
  Why:  Graftcode publishes a small CLAUDE.md router plus per-language rules read on demand (grft-dev/graftcode-demos).
  askai:       askai plugins info graftcode

Memory plugins
  Rule: Use at most one memory tool; the handoff file and project files are usually enough.
  Why:  No independent measurement for claude-mem or Supermemory; both add context to sessions.
  askai:       askai plugins info claude-mem

Context7 and Repomix
  Rule: Context7 for current library docs when needed; Repomix only for handovers between tools, narrowed to the folders that matter.
  Why:  A full repository snapshot is large; symbol search reads less.
  askai:       askai plugins install context7 | repomix

Aider
  Rule: A separate coding agent, not a plugin: run it in its own session and never on the same files as another agent.
  Why:  Its /architect mode separates planning from editing, like AskAI's lead and build tiers.

Codex subagent models
  Rule: Ask for custom agents by name and check the model they really ran.
  Why:  Codex never spawns custom agents by itself; a reported bug lets in-app workers inherit the parent model (GitHub openai/codex #32587).
  Codex        Spawn runner for <task>
  askai:       askai infra shows models used

Antigravity agent models
  Rule: Agent files take only a tier: flash, pro, flash_lite or inherit; set effort per session.
  Why:  Any other model value makes Antigravity skip the agent file silently (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli #1270).
  Antigravity  /effort high
  askai:       askai init writes model: flash

Cursor models and plans
  Rule: Free and Plus: Grok 4.7 and Composer only; Sonnet needs Premium or above (billed at API price).
  Why:  Cursor help, Available models (2026).
  Cursor       agent models
  askai:       askai models set cursor.useSonnet true

Seeing what each plugin saves
  Rule: askai savings runs each installed plugin's own report (rtk gain, ccusage daily, headroom perf, codebase-memory projects, Graphify graph status); askai plugins info <id> shows the in-agent commands.
  Why:  Tools report their own estimates; RTK's counter showed 96M saved during runs that cost more. Compare with askai usage and askai audit.
  askai:       askai savings 7; askai usage 7

Shorter replies
  Rule: On by default: the terse rule (Caveman-style), the diff-only rule, Codex verbosity low, and the output line in askai prompt. For one task: askai prompt --output diff.
  Why:  Output tokens cost about five times input on Claude; Caveman-style replies measured about 8% cheaper (median of six studies).
  askai:       askai prompt --output diff; --caveman ultra for the shortest replies

Things only you can do
  Rule: askai todo lists every manual step per tool and repository; checkable ones clear themselves.
  Why:  A plugin that is installed but never set up costs tokens without saving any.
  askai:       askai todo; askai todo done <id>

Security habits
  Rule: No secrets in prompts or files; treat tool output and web text as untrusted; approve destructive commands; read installer scripts; no proxies you do not control.
  Why:  Agents act on what they read; a pasted key or an injected instruction costs far more than tokens.
  askai:       askai guide security; .env reads denied; askai check flags billing variables

Base command-line tools
  Rule: Have rg, jq and gh installed: targeted search and JSON queries replace whole-file reads, gh replaces a GitHub MCP server.
  Why:  Reads were about 90% of tool-result tokens in one measured workload (Marmelab).
  askai:       askai install --base-tools

Prompt patterns by task
  Rule: Bug: reproduce, root cause, minimal fix, regression test. Feature: acceptance criteria, small verified steps. Design: options first, no code. Risky: approval before destructive steps.
  Why:  A pattern that fits the task avoids the most expensive turns: rework and wrong paths.
  askai:       askai prompt --kind bug|feature|design|risky
